Rakamaz Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Rakamaz, Hungary

Demolished. Jews settled in Rakamaz in the second half of the 18th century; the formal community, established in 1840 with 113 members, grew to 170 by 1930. From 1885, the Orthodox community's rabbi doubled as Vencsellő's rabbi; by the 1944 deportations, no rabbi remained, only a shochet and synagogue caretaker. In April 1944, residents were confined to the synagogue before being transported by cart to Tokaj, then the Sátoraljaújhely Ghetto, and finally Auschwitz. This cemetery, documented on an 1870 cadastral map, was demolished at an unrecorded time.
